title: audio_features.json — tempo, beats, onsets, envelopes, loudness, vocal activity
description: All dense series use the timeseries convention (common.schema.json) at a 10 ms hop and are sampled at arbitrary t via linear interpolation; beats/onsets are sorted event lists queried by binary search. This document owns the beat grid: every beat/bar index anywhere in the library refers to it.

bpm_global.description: Single representative tempo. Tempo drift shows up in the beat grid itself, not here. Always > 0: a mix with no beat evidence (digital silence, or no beats tracked) fails the features stage (manifest status failed) instead of writing a document, so consumers may divide by this value.

confidence.description: Onset support for the beat grid, in [0, 1]. For beat i at frame b_i with local period p_i (the following inter-beat interval; the last beat reuses the previous one), on_i = max of the mix onset-strength envelope within ±30 ms of b_i and off_i = the smallest of the same ±30 ms max at the six probes b_i + k·p_i/7, k = 1..6 (a probe whose ±30 ms window would contain b_i or the next beat is skipped). The 1/7-beat points coincide with no common subdivision (8ths, swung 8ths, triplets, 16ths, quintuplets, sextuplets), so at least one probe reads the gap between subdivision hits and subdivided rhythms under a correct grid still count as rhythmic; septuplet subdivisions are the blind spot. confidence = mean over beats of clip((on_i − off_i) / ref, 0, 1), ref = 90th percentile of on_i; 0.0 when fewer than 2 beats. Beatless material (drones, noise) scores about 0.1-0.25; beats placed over silence count 0; a clean click track scores ~0.9. Below ~0.5 treat the whole grid as advisory. It does NOT detect half- or double-tempo errors: a grid at half (or twice) the true tempo still sits on onsets and can score high.

beats.description: The unified beat grid. Beat index i = times[i]. Beats span only the tracked rhythmic region: beatless intros and outros carry no beats (the tracker trims leading/trailing beats over weak onset strength); interior breakdowns are not trimmed. Bar index of beat i = floor((i - downbeat_offset) / beats_per_bar) for i >= downbeat_offset; bar index clamps to 0 for beats before the first downbeat.

downbeat_offset.description: Index into times of the first downbeat; downbeats are then every beats_per_bar-th beat. With fewer than beats_per_bar beats no phase fit runs and this is 0.

downbeat_method.description: assumed_4_4_phase_fit = estimated by choosing the beat phase maximizing onset strength under a 4/4 assumption; consumers should treat bar indices as approximate. 'model' reserved for a future real downbeat tracker.

integrated_lufs.description: EBU R128 integrated loudness of the mix; use to normalize levels across tracks. A fully silent program is clamped to -70.0 (the R128 absolute gate). Input shorter than one 400 ms gating block is measured as a single block spanning the whole signal.

stems.description: Fixed four Demucs stems — fixed keys so Swift decodes a concrete struct.

vocal_activity.description: Regions where the vocal stem is active, from hysteresis thresholding of its RMS envelope. lyrics.json measures its coverage against these.

params.description: The hysteresis parameters that produced these regions — embedded (per the schema README params policy) so a consumer can compare regions across tracks analyzed under different settings.

enter_db.description: Vocal-stem RMS (dBFS) above which a region opens.

exit_db.description: RMS below which an open region closes.

min_gap_seconds.description: Regions closer than this are merged.

mean_rms_db.description: Mean vocal-stem RMS within the region, dBFS.

spectral_centroid_hz.description: unit 'hz'. Frames below the silence floor hold the last valid centroid (frames before the first valid one are backfilled from it), so the series is everywhere-interpolable with no sentinel values. A channel that is silent throughout (e.g. the vocals stem of an instrumental) writes 0.0 for the entire series — check rms_db before using centroid. Whether anything is playing is rms_db's job, not this field's.

strengths.description: Parallel to times, same length; raw onset-envelope value divided by strength_reference, clamped to [0, 1]. Only onsets that pass the level gate (see gate) are listed; the strength itself is level-independent (the onset envelope is a ratio measure), so a quiet part's onsets are not weaker than a loud part's. The robust (p98) reference keeps values comparable across tracks: 'drum strength > 0.6' means roughly the same thing everywhere, and one outlier accent cannot compress the rest toward 0.

strength_reference.description: 98th percentile of this channel's raw onset-strength envelope (the whole envelope, before gating) — the normalization denominator, in raw envelope units. Raw strength of onset i = strengths[i] * strength_reference. When times is empty (no onset survived detection and gating — always so for a channel whose rms_db sits at the -80.0 floor throughout, e.g. a silent or dither-only stem), the documented sentinel 1.0 is written so the field stays present and positive.

gate.description: The level gate that selected these onsets, embedded so onset lists can be compared across tracks analyzed under different settings. Detected onsets are dropped when this channel's published rms_db at the onset frame is at floor_db, and (stems only) when the stem's rms_db minus the mix's rms_db at that frame is below relative_db — separation bleed and dither are otherwise reported as full-strength onsets. Absent in 1.0.0 documents (ungated).

floor_db.description: rms_db silence floor (dBFS); onsets in frames at or below it are dropped.

relative_db.description: Stems only (absent on the mix): minimum stem-minus-mix rms_db (dB) at the onset frame for the onset to be kept.
